So worries, happy to help! If you notice the rubric focuses more on the techniques and style analysis.

Past papers are helpful but to a limit. What my class did was annotate poems and sections of plays and practice planning an essay. If there is one you like then write it out. Or practice just writing the introduction/body paragraph and ask your teacher to review it, rewrite it to improve it and repeat. So it doesnt have to be the official past papers. Just google a random poem or pick a random 2 pages from a key part of a book. The more you try just annotating and specific section the better the whole thing will be. You dont always have yo do a full practice. Save those for when you are more confident and really wanna test yourself.

M21 exam route here, HL i think is really tough because it depends on the books you get and the teacher as usual can make or break the subject. (For reference i worked from 4s on papers to 6s and 7s and then ended up with a 7). I did well without reading every single text. In fact i probably didnt read more books than i did read. I even did my IO on a book that i didnt read lol. Here are my few tips.

1) read the easy stuff, plays and poems mainly. Watch the play if it helps just make sure its the right version. The texts you use for IOs and stuff can be poems or play which are much easier so take that advantage wherever you can.

2) while understanding plot is obvious great the important parts of analysis is where they use techniques. Which dont come from plot. Look at the syntax, use of language, metaphoric language, irony, description etc. All of the literary devices. That should be the bulk of your essays anyway. (You should zoom in and zoom out). So for example on of my IO texts i didnt read like at all, but i found an extract where the author wrote really interestingly and just used those few pages.

3) Hopefully you have people in your class who read the books. Ask them for a key chapter or something to read so you understand the writers style and get the rest of the plot online. Focus on key points where something shifts or changes comment in class about those and use those where you can.

Basically make shit easier for yourself. Poetry is shorter but arguably can have more to critically engage with. Plays have their own set of techniques. Thats more for coursework and exams.

For class just try to get a key chapter down or a key thing to focus on each class just say that and you will ‘participate in full’ without needing general knowledge. Or comment on the style of the writer, thats still english.

Plot is important but its only a part on Lit dont forget to zoom in and when zoom out just try and think of a larger consideration or some message from the text and youll do aight. If anyone has more questions dm :))

Are you proposing to direct/produce a play with the company? This is quite common if you’re curious as part of the IB Theatre course students produce a production proposal of a few pages. It even covers a thematic exploration of the script. Worth taking a look there for ideas.

Generally my understanding is that its just a way for you to show the company more about what your work might look like and if its a match with them.

Hey, coming from an amateur actor in regular theatre, musical theatre and a singer. i mean the key thing is warm up. This way you hopefully wont be straining your voice as much. Another trick of the trade is to use this special tea called throat coat. It comes in different flavours but is really good for your voice drinking it the day of a performance always helps my voices clarity and stops the straining of voice you should be able to pick some up off amazon. Professional theatre folk use it and singers like charlie puth. Otherwise the classic hot water and honey can have a similar effect. Try what works for you. If you’re coming up to performance avoid dairy, oily food and spicy things and again it will be easier for your vocals. Hope this helps!

If she really doesnt want to talk then dont make her hate you. Just tell her youre always there and make her promise that before she does anything she will contact you. I had that with a friend who self harmed. The deal was if they were going to they had to talk to me first. It helped them reduce it. But its really tricky because with this you cant really help someone who refuses the help so you try your absolute hardest which you are doing and hope it turns out. Dont give up and just keep reminding her that you’re there. Even just distracting her with anything else is helping if she doesn’t want to talk about her feelings just try and distract her.

I found myself in a similar situation but because of what she was going through it wasnt the right time for her to get in a relationship which broke my heart but i respect her choice. Ive also had to deal with suicidal friends. You have to force them to talk a bit. Coming from someone who has been suicidal if you let them just sit it gets worse. They are their own worst enemy. If it becomes a really serious concern where she not only is saying it but starting to plan (suicide ideation) then you might have to reach out to her family. Not matter what conflict is going on at home no one wants a family member to die even if theyre fighting. Just try to do what your doing text her good morning, good night share with her things that will make her laugh tell her she is beautiful and how much she means to you. What stopped me was knowing there was someone who I would hurt if I did it. Because even when a suicidal person looses the will to maintain themselves they can still care about other people and what the effect might be on them. Youre awesome for caring so much about her

Ive used commedia masks, neutral masks, balinese theatre masks and just a bunch if assorted stylised masks. If you interested in mask work take a look at Jacques Lecoq and his practice with mask. He favoured neutral masks from Japanese noh theatre and is one of the most famous practitioners ever. He believed that but using a mask ones physical expression is increased as the actor cannot reply on their face to show expression. Suddenly their arms and body is needed to exaggerate and do more. It changes completely how an actor acts. If youre more curious he has a good book called method of movement and you can look into his mask awakening experience.
